questions.stem: Write the initiation step for the chlorination of methane, including the condition.
questions.modelAnswer: Cl2 -> 2Cl•, initiated by ultraviolet light splitting the halogen molecule homolytically.

questions.stem: Define a free radical and state the notation used for it.
questions.modelAnswer: A free radical is a species with an unpaired electron, represented by a single dot after the symbol.

questions.stem: Explain why ultraviolet light is required for initiation but not for the propagation steps.
questions.modelAnswer: Breaking the Cl-Cl bond homolytically needs the photon's energy input, whereas the propagation reactions release energy through new bond formation and run spontaneously once radicals exist.

questions.stem: Bromine is used instead of chlorine in a radical substitution. Write the initiation step with correct notation and name the condition.
questions.modelAnswer: Br2 -> 2Br• under ultraviolet light: the halogen molecule splits homolytically into two bromine radicals, each carrying its unpaired electron as a dot.

questions.stem: Write both propagation steps of methane chlorination with radical dots.
questions.modelAnswer: Step one: Cl• + CH4 -> CH3• + HCl; step two: CH3• + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + Cl•.

questions.stem: State what is meant by a chain reaction in this context.
questions.modelAnswer: A chain reaction is the alternating propagation sequence in which each stroke consumes one radical and regenerates another, letting the substitution run thousands of times from one initiation event.

questions.stem: Explain why the propagation steps' sum equals the overall substitution equation.
questions.modelAnswer: Adding the two strokes cancels the radical intermediates - Cl• appears as reactant then product, CH3• likewise - leaving only CH4 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + HCl.

questions.stem: Write the two propagation steps for the bromination of methane and sum them.
questions.modelAnswer: Br• + CH4 -> CH3• + HBr; CH3• + Br2 -> CH3Br + Br•; the sum is CH4 + Br2 -> CH3Br + HBr with both radicals cancelled.

questions.stem: Write two termination equations for the methane chlorination mixture.
questions.modelAnswer: Cl• + Cl• -> Cl2 and CH3• + CH3• -> C2H6 (with CH3• + Cl• -> CH3Cl also possible).

questions.stem: List the substitution series methane follows under excess chlorine.
questions.modelAnswer: CH4 -> CH3Cl -> CH2Cl2 -> CHCl3 -> CCl4, each step replacing one hydrogen.

questions.stem: Explain why a single unreactive molecule forms in each termination step.
questions.modelAnswer: Each radical carries one unpaired electron, so two radicals together supply exactly one shared pair - their combination forms one complete, paired, therefore unreactive molecule.

questions.stem: A termination event pairs two methyl radicals. Write the equation and show that the atom ledger closes.
questions.modelAnswer: CH3• + CH3• -> C2H6: the two radicals together carry 2 carbons and 6 hydrogens, and the ethane product holds exactly 2 C and 6 H, so the ledger closes on both sides.
